newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Powerful bomb kills at least three in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Powerful bomb kills at least three in Colombia.

text.p: A powerful bomb blast tore through a building in the centre of Colombia's northwest city of Medellin on Wednesday, killing at least three people and leaving about 30 seriously injured, authorities said.

Gen. Luis Ernesto Gilibert, deputy director of the National Police, said the explosion, which occurred at 11:20 a.m. EST (1620 GMT), was caused by a remote-controlled bomb comprised of about 155 pounds (70 kg) of dynmaite.
The deadly device was detonated under the second-story stairway of a building housing a popular eatery called La Sorpresa and a Medellin civic group known as Asocomunal, Gilibert said.

Police sources said the building also housed the offices of a right-wing paramilitary group, indicating that leftist guerrillas may be responsible for the bomb. But Gilibert, who spoke in an interview from the scene with the Radionet radio news network, said that was not confirmed.
The blast occurred a short distance away from one of Medellin's largest companies, Empresas Publicas de Medellin, and its president, Mauricio Restrepo, described it as "extremely powerful."
"The shock wave moved us all off our seats," he added.
Police said three people were killed in the explosion and about 30 injured. The identities of the dead were not immeidiately available.

Medellin, which has Colombia's highest rate of violent crime, is often described as the murder capital of the world. Gunmen of the left and right have killed with impunity in the city for years and it was a hotbed of bomb attacks and political assassinations in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when authorities were waging war with the now defunct Medellin drug cartel.
